# How major US stock indexes fared Monday 6/1/2026

Oil prices rose following the latest fighting to threaten the U.S.-Iran ceasefire, but Wall Street isn’t very worried, and U.S. stocks rose to more records

June 1, 2026

By Associated Press

Oil prices rose following the latest fighting to threaten the U.S.-Iran ceasefire, but Wall Street isn’t very worried, and U.S. stocks rose to more records.

The S&P 500 added 0.3% Monday to its prior all-time high. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.1%, and the Nasdaq composite gained 0.4%, both also adding to their previous records set last week.

The price for a barrel of Brent crude rose more than 4%, which pushed up Treasury yields and hurt companies with big fuel bills. But strong profit reports from U.S. companies and continued strength for big technology stocks kept Wall Street’s momentum going.

On Monday:

The S&P 500 rose 19.90 points, or 0.3%, to 7,599.96.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 46.42 points, or 0.1%, to 51,078.88.

The Nasdaq composite rose 114.19 points, or 0.4%, to 27,086.81.

The Russell 2000 index of smaller companies fell 13.58 points, or 0.5% to 2,905.76.

For the year:

The S&P 500 is up 754.46 points, or 11%.

The Dow is up 3,015.59 points, or 6.3%.

The Nasdaq is up 3,844.82 points, or 16.5%.

The Russell 2000 is up 423.86 points, or 17.1%.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

U.S. stocks ticked to the edge of records as Wall Street’s momentum keeps pushing it upward.

### Entry 179 (1 OCT): internal contradiction

Published claim 24/7 Wall St.’s closing card for Thursday, marked “As seen on the 24/7 Wall St. homepage on October 1, 2026” with no time, was headlined “S&P 500 Closes at 7,678 as Growth Leads on Quarter-Open Day,” over a body that says “The S&P 500 closed at 7,678.25, up about 0.34%” and “the S&P 500 finished at 7,678.25 while the Dow ended red.” The table on the same card, labelled “At close,” has the S&P 500 at 7,686.00, up 0.17 percent, the Dow at 51,030.80 and the Russell 2000 at 2,815.81.

Desk assessment The S&P 500 closed at 7,666.45, up 14.91, or 0.19 percent, the Dow at 50,926.56, up 20.51, and the Russell 2000 at 2,806.63 (the Associated Press’s table; BBN Times; Schwab). The Dow did not end red. Two closes on one card, 7.75 points apart, and neither is the close: they miss it by 11.80 and 19.55 points. The headline’s level and change are the ones a data provider’s page attached to its contract on Thursday evening (entry 171). ### Entry 171 (1 OCT): internal contradiction

Published claim A data provider’s United States index page, read between 7:17 and 7:29 p.m. and again between 7:37 and 7:48 p.m. Thursday, showed the S&P 500 at 7,677.05 beside a change of 14.91, 0.19 percent, and the Dow at 50,956.55 beside 20.51, 0.04 percent, both dated 1 October, under a sentence saying the index “rose to 7678 points on October 1, 2026, gaining 0.34% from the previous session.”

How major US stock indexes fared Monday 6/1/2026
Date: Mon Jun  1 20:24:28 2026 UTC

Oil prices rose following the latest fighting to threaten the U.S.-Iran ceasefire, but Wall Street isn't very worried, and U.S. stocks rose to more records. 
The S&P 500 added 0.3% Monday to its prior all-time high. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.1%, and the Nasdaq composite gained 0.4%, both also adding to their previous records set last week. 
The price for a barrel of Brent crude rose more than 4%, which pushed up Treasury yields and hurt companies with big fuel bills. But strong profit reports from U.S. companies and continued strength for big technology stocks kept Wall Street's momentum going.
On Monday:
The S&P 500 rose 19.90 points, or 0.3%, to 7,599.96.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 46.42 points, or 0.1%, to 51,078.88.
The Nasdaq composite rose 114.19 points, or 0.4%, to 27,086.81.
The Russell 2000 index of smaller companies fell 13.58 points, or 0.5% to 2,905.76.
